reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism of sleep-induced hallucination arises from a sudden collapse in top-down cortical inhibition, allowing lower motor centers to reach a 'tonic tension explosion point'. This is modeled as a dynamical system where inhibition I(t) drops below a critical threshold, causing a feedback loop in sensory processing. The disruption of normal associative pathways leads to unregulated activation A(t), which amplifies sensory signals S(t) beyond their original intensity. The system exhibits a bifurcation point where small peripheral inputs I_p can trigger large-scale sensory experiences S_d. The failure mode occurs when the resistance R(t) to activation drops below a critical value, leading to runaway sensory amplification without contextual modulation. This aligns with known neurophysiology of REM sleep and altered consciousness states.
